cookies.instructions:
1. Install the "Get cookies.txt LOCALLY" extension in your browser (Chrome / Firefox / Edge).

2. Open a new private / incognito window and sign in to YouTube.

3. In the same window and same tab, navigate to: https://www.youtube.com/robots.txt (this must be the only private/incognito tab open)

4. Click the extension icon and export your cookies ("Export as cookies.txt"), then close the private window so the session is never reopened in the browser.

5. Place the cookies.txt file at the application root: {cookies_dir}

6. Restart the download.

YouTube rotates cookies on open browser tabs. Using a private window ensures exported cookies stay valid.

error.drm_protected:
This content is protected by DRM and cannot be downloaded.

DRM (Digital Rights Management) prevents downloading from services like Spotify, Netflix, etc.
error.http_403:
YouTube refused the download (HTTP Error 403: Forbidden).

This is usually a temporary block triggered by YouTube's bot detection. It is not caused by the playlist itself.

Tips:
- Wait a while (15-30 min) and try again.
- Avoid downloading many videos in quick succession.
- Using browser cookies often helps.

format.template_info_text:
{title} — Video title
{artist} — Channel name / artist
{album} — Album name (if available)
{tracknumber} — Track number in playlist
 — Extension (mp3, mp4, opus)

Date:
{Y} — 4-digit year (2026)
{y} — 2-digit year (26)
{m} — Month (04)
{d} — Day (24)
{B} — Full month name (April)
{b} — Abbreviated month (Apr)

Time:
{H} — 24-hour (02, 17)
{M} — Minute (17)
{S} — Second (31)

Use / to create subdirectories.

Examples:
{Y}-{m}-{d} - {artist} - {title}.
→ 2026-04-24 - ArtistName - SongTitle.mp3

{d} {B} {Y} - {title}.
→ 24 April 2026 - SongTitle.mp3

options.enrich_tooltip:
Enriches audio metadata by querying several online sources:
• MusicBrainz: album info, artist, genre, release date
• Cover Art Archive: high-resolution album artwork
• LRCLIB: synchronized lyrics (LRC)
• Genius: lyrics (text)
options.normalize_tooltip:
LUFS normalization adjusts the volume to reach a precise loudness target.

-14 LUFS is the standard of streaming platforms (Spotify, YouTube Music).
Lower values (e.g. -18) give a softer sound; higher values (e.g. -10) make it louder but may cause clipping.
